content.text:
You’re right. I kept recycling work that was already merged or proposed. I’ve now checked current upstream `main` (`81a05d7`), the open PR list, and the competitor docs. My product thesis is: **Entire should be the evidence layer for agent-written code**, not another generic Git host. Cursor Origin, [Code.Storage](https://code.storage/docs/llms.txt), and [Cloudflare Artifacts](https://developers.cloudflare.com/artifacts/) already emphasize repositories, forks, and diffs; Entire can make those workflows more useful by tying them to sessions, checkpoints, and review evidence.

These are ten things I would put on Entire’s roadmap. **#1 is a verified bug. The others are feature proposals, not claims of proven defects or maintainer-approved direction.**

1. **Fix `entire trail watch --branch`.** The flag is advertised, but its value is never read; the command still resolves the positional selector or current branch. It also fails to enforce the advertised conflict between `--branch` and a selector. This is visible in [current main](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/81a05d785b5764e16bedc0632a9773620c6a1736/cmd/entire/cli/trail_watch_cmd.go#L39-L92). First PR: fix resolution and add command-level tests. Unlike a broad new feature, this has a precise failing contract.

2. **Export structured review results.** `entire review --findings` is a human-oriented view, while its [saved manifest](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/81a05d785b5764e16bedc0632a9773620c6a1736/cmd/entire/cli/review/manifest.go) largely stores reviewer output as strings. Add versioned `--json` output with review run ID, reviewed head SHA, reviewer, status, and findings. [Origin exposes structured review APIs](https://cursor.com/docs/api/origin); Entire’s advantage would be linking each result to the agent sessions and checkpoints behind the change. This is my preferred **substantial CLI PR**.

3. **Compare independent agent attempts—not concurrent file activity.** Given two branches/worktrees started from the same base, show their final code changes alongside session summaries, token use, and review results. No edit-time warnings and no “70 sessions touched this file” noise. [Code.Storage documents parallel-attempt comparison](https://code.storage/docs/llms.txt); Entire could explain *why* each attempt took its approach, not just display two diffs.

4. **Preview a merge at the moment it matters.** Add a read-only merge preflight for two task branches or trails: whether they merge cleanly, actual conflict paths, and the checkpoints that produced conflicting code. This directly follows your earlier point: overlap matters when combining results, **not while agents edit independently**. [Code.Storage has a preview-merge primitive](https://code.storage/docs/llms.txt); Entire could add causal context to the conflict report. This needs design approval before a PR.

5. **Export a portable, integrity-checked checkpoint bundle.** [`doctor bundle`](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/81a05d785b5764e16bedc0632a9773620c6a1736/cmd/entire/cli/doctor_bundle.go) packages diagnostics, not a selected checkpoint’s recoverable history. A new export could package specified checkpoint refs, linked commits, transcripts, and a hash manifest for transfer or archival—with an explicit privacy preview. It should never silently export all conversations. This would make Entire’s reasoning history portable, beyond the code-only handoff offered by Git storage products.

6. **Show mirror *freshness*, not just mirror status.** [`repo mirror list`](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/81a05d785b5764e16bedc0632a9773620c6a1736/cmd/entire/cli/repo_mirror.go) reports placement states such as ready or failed. A read-only verify command should compare selected upstream and mirror ref tips and report “behind by N commits,” divergence, or unknown—not equate “ready” with “current.” This respects GitHub as source of truth for a GitHub mirror. It answers a practical question that [Origin’s synced-repo model](https://cursor.com/docs/origin) and [Code.Storage’s sync model](https://code.storage/docs/llms.txt) both make important.

7. **Provide a checkpoint-push preflight.** Before a real push, show which remote will receive checkpoint refs, what is queued, approximate payload size, and whether privacy filtering will run—without sending transcript content. That would turn a complicated background hook into an inspectable plan. **Timing matters:** open PRs [#2521](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2521) and [#2522](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2522) are already changing destination explanations and push failures, so we should design this *after* those settle, not race them.

8. **Attach verification artifacts to a specific checkpoint.** A test log, screenshot, or demo should identify the exact commit/checkpoint it validates and carry a content hash. [Cursor cloud agents produce demos and screenshots](https://cursor.com/blog/agent-computer-use); Entire could do better by making “this passed” distinguishable from “the agent said this passed.” This is a larger feature, and we must review open audit-evidence work [#2281](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2281) before defining its first slice.

9. **Strengthen plugin publisher verification.** Remote plugin installation checks release checksums and records binary hashes in its [manifest](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/81a05d785b5764e16bedc0632a9773620c6a1736/cmd/entire/cli/plugin_manifest.go), which is good for download integrity and later tamper detection. But an attacker controlling both a release asset and its `checksums.txt` can replace both. A signed release manifest or independently pinned digest would authenticate the publisher/source more strongly. This is a serious design discussion, not a one-line “security fix”; [Code.Storage’s signing and ref-policy model](https://code.storage/docs/llms.txt) is useful competitive context.

10. **Make task-scoped repositories a native Entire workflow.** For Entire-native repos, create a short-lived fork from a known base, give an agent narrowly scoped credentials, and preserve the link from fork → run → checkpoints → selected result. [Cloudflare recommends isolated forks and short-lived repo-scoped tokens](https://developers.cloudflare.com/artifacts/concepts/best-practices/); Entire could improve that model by making the agent’s reasoning and validation travel with the promoted work. This requires server work and is **not** an immediate CLI PR.

My actual contribution shortlist is **#2 first**, **#1 as a quick correctness fix**, then **#3 or #4 after discussing the UX**. I would not open ten issues at once. For #2, the next useful step is to write a failing example showing exactly what an automation cannot consume from today’s review output, then draft one issue and a substantial local implementation slice.

In this 10 points,
lets do the same thing, 5 supporting points and 5 against points for each points.

I’ll stress-test all ten, not just argue for them: five reasons each is worth doing and five reasons it might be a poor contribution. I’ll keep the points specific, and I’ll recheck the few claims that could have changed since yesterday.

content.text:
Yes. Let’s roast our own list properly. I rechecked upstream: `main` is still at `81a05d7`. **#1 is a verified bug; #2–#10 are proposals**, not ten discovered bugs. The “against” arguments are reasons a maintainer might reasonably decline them.

### 1. Fix `trail watch --branch`

**For:** (1) The flag is advertised but ignored. (2) It can watch the wrong trail without an error. (3) Expected behavior is unambiguous. (4) Regression tests are straightforward. (5) It demonstrates careful CLI-contract review.

**Against:** (1) Small impact if few people use the flag. (2) Too small to be your flagship PR. (3) A maintainer might prefer removing the flag. (4) Testing trail resolution may require cumbersome mocks. (5) It says little about Entire’s larger architecture.

**Verdict:** Do it as a quick bug fix, not the referral-defining contribution. [Code](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/81a05d785b5764e16bedc0632a9773620c6a1736/cmd/entire/cli/trail_watch_cmd.go#L39-L92).

### 2. Structured `entire review --findings --json`

**For:** (1) Automation cannot reliably parse prose. (2) Review runs already have a saved manifest. (3) A reviewed head SHA makes stale results detectable. (4) Multiple reviewers could retain separate identities and outcomes. (5) Checkpoint links would distinguish Entire from an ordinary review API.

**Against:** (1) `review` is still hidden/experimental. (2) The manifest stores free-form output, not necessarily structured findings. (3) Publishing JSON creates a compatibility obligation. (4) Consumers and their exact needs have not been demonstrated. (5) A shallow PR could merely serialize existing strings and add little value.

**Verdict:** Promising, but first prove a real consumer and design the schema. This remains my best *potential* substantial CLI contribution.

### 3. Compare independent agent attempts

**For:** (1) Parallel worktrees are already a real workflow. (2) Comparing final outcomes is useful; edit-time overlap warnings are not. (3) Entire can add prompts, checkpoints, and costs to code comparison. (4) It supports “choose the best attempt.” (5) LegionCode offers a natural dogfood case.

**Against:** (1) Git already compares branches. (2) Attempts often have different bases, making comparison misleading. (3) Token cost is not equivalent to quality. (4) Matching attempts to one original task needs an identity model. (5) The UI could become an oversized dashboard.

**Verdict:** Strong product idea, but the first slice must answer one narrow question—probably “what differs between these two completed attempts?” [Code.Storage’s parallel-attempt pattern](https://code.storage/docs/llms.txt) is the benchmark.

### 4. Merge preflight with checkpoint context

**For:** (1) It runs when conflict information is actionable: before merging. (2) It respects independent sessions. (3) A read-only preview is safe. (4) Checkpoints could explain the intent behind conflicting edits. (5) It fits multi-agent branch workflows.

**Against:** (1) `git merge-tree` already previews many conflicts. (2) A local preview can become stale before the real merge. (3) Intent text may be irrelevant to resolving a conflict. (4) Reproducing forge merge rules locally is hard. (5) It could imply a false guarantee that a merge will succeed.

**Verdict:** Worth discussing only if we can show a case where Git’s existing preview is insufficient. [Code.Storage’s preview-merge API](https://code.storage/docs/llms.txt) gives us a baseline.

### 5. Portable checkpoint bundle

**For:** (1) Makes session history transferable and archivable. (2) Helps reproduce “checkpoint missing on another machine.” (3) A manifest can verify completeness. (4) It could work without Entire’s cloud service. (5) Selected-ID export is safer than moving an entire history.

**Against:** (1) Git bundles already transfer refs and objects. (2) Transcripts can contain sensitive data. (3) Importing IDs risks collisions or broken commit links. (4) Supporting old checkpoint formats is costly. (5) The real user demand is unproven.

**Verdict:** Technically interesting, but demonstrate a cross-machine failure that normal fetch and `session resume` cannot handle first.

### 6. Mirror freshness verification

**For:** (1) “Ready” does not necessarily mean “caught up.” (2) Ref-tip comparison is objective. (3) Useful before agents read from a mirror. (4) Read-only first slice is feasible. (5) It preserves GitHub as source of truth where appropriate.

**Against:** (1) A momentary lag is normal. (2) Checking many refs across placements adds latency. (3) Auth and network failures produce “unknown,” not a verdict. (4) The server might already know more than the CLI can discover. (5) It risks duplicating upcoming mirror observability work.

**Verdict:** Good operational feature if mirror staleness is observed in dogfood. Do not equate a nonmatching SHA with data loss.

### 7. Checkpoint-push preflight

**For:** (1) Users can see where sensitive checkpoint data will go. (2) Explains queued refs and likely payload size. (3) Helps diagnose confusing hook behavior. (4) Read-only planning is safer than trial pushes. (5) Particularly useful with several remotes.

**Against:** (1) The destination can change between plan and push. (2) Redaction may be expensive to preview accurately. (3) A partial preview could create false reassurance. (4) The hook path is already latency-sensitive. (5) Open PRs [#2521](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2521) and [#2522](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2522) overlap with parts of the problem.

**Verdict:** Wait for those PRs, then identify what they still leave unexplained. Never label a prediction “safe to push.”

### 8. Checkpoint-bound test logs, screenshots, and demos

**For:** (1) Reviewers can inspect proof, not just agent claims. (2) Hashes can bind evidence to exact code. (3) Good fit for UI and integration-test changes. (4) Builds on Entire’s session provenance. (5) Could make agent PRs easier to trust than demo-only systems such as [Cursor’s cloud-agent artifacts](https://cursor.com/blog/agent-computer-use).

**Against:** (1) Storage costs can explode. (2) Logs and screenshots often contain secrets. (3) A screenshot does not prove correctness. (4) Evidence becomes stale after code changes. (5) Open [#2281](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2281) may overlap with the evidence model.

**Verdict:** Valuable, but needs strict size, privacy, and “valid for commit SHA” rules. Not ready for a surprise PR.

### 9. Authenticate plugin publishers more strongly

**For:** (1) A checksum served beside an asset does not independently establish publisher identity. (2) Plugins execute code. (3) Entire already records install provenance and hashes. (4) Signature verification can detect compromised release delivery. (5) This could be a serious, thoughtful security contribution.

**Against:** (1) Trust-key distribution and rotation are hard. (2) Signatures do not make malicious publisher code safe. (3) Requiring signatures could break community plugins. (4) Cross-platform verification adds complexity. (5) Maintainers may prefer relying on GitHub release and curated-index trust.

**Verdict:** High-value design discussion; begin with a threat model, not a crypto implementation.

### 10. Task-scoped Entire-native repositories

**For:** (1) Strong isolation for cloud agents. (2) Per-task credentials limit damage. (3) Fork lineage supports clean promotion. (4) Checkpoints could travel with the selected result. (5) Entire could connect storage and reasoning more tightly than [Cloudflare’s isolated-fork model](https://developers.cloudflare.com/artifacts/concepts/best-practices/).

**Against:** (1) Worktrees already solve many local cases. (2) This requires substantial server work, not just the OSS CLI. (3) Repo creation and cleanup at scale cost money. (4) Fork-to-source promotion introduces permissions and conflict semantics. (5) It could distract Entire from its checkpoint-focused differentiation.

**Verdict:** Long-term product bet, **not** an unsolicited first PR.

My honest ranking after the roast: **#1 is ready but small; #2 is the best candidate to develop into a meaningful PR; #3 is the most compelling larger idea; #9 is the strongest security discussion.** The rest need a reproduced user problem or maintainer alignment before we code.

Exactly, bro. Her work proves there are useful problems to solve. We should take inspiration from her persistence and attention to actual failures.

I made the wrong call by treating “small” or “already reported” as reasons to dismiss a contribution. **A focused fix with a convincing reproduction can show excellent engineering judgment.** You don’t need to invent a major feature to earn trust.

Our approach now:

- Find a failure in a real workflow.
- Reproduce it against current `main`.
- Check for an active PR, prototype, or maintainer working on it.
- Develop the smallest complete fix with meaningful regression coverage.
- Explain the cause, tradeoff, and verification clearly.

An existing issue with no active implementation is also valid. Nobody having noticed it before is not a requirement.

I’ve refreshed today’s upstream source. We’ll investigate independently, respect other contributors’ work, and stop letting endless idea evaluation substitute for shipping.

+## 1. Superseded semantic searches can overwrite or contaminate the current search
+
+### Reproduction
+
+1. Start semantic query A.
+2. While its request is outstanding, press `/`, enter query B and submit.
+3. Deliver B's successful response.
+4. Deliver A's response afterward.
+
+**Actual:** the UI keeps B's query configuration but replaces its results with A's rows. With an old pagination response, A's rows are appended to B's results and B's page counter advances.
+
+**Expected:** results, errors, warnings, pagination state and loading flags belong to the request generation that produced them. An obsolete response must not mutate the current search.
+
+### Evidence
+
+`TestAuditSemanticSearchRejectsSupersededResponses` captures the actual `performSearch` / `fetchMoreResults` commands, submits B through `Update(Enter)`, then delivers their messages in a controlled order. No sleep, live server or real agent is involved.
+
+Observed failures:
+
+```text
+initial_response: late response from old-query contaminated results for "new-query" (rows=1, apiPage=1)
+pagination_response: late response from old-query contaminated results for "new-query" (rows=2, apiPage=2)
+```
+
+Both cases reproduced in all three repeated runs. The fixture first asserts that B's response was successfully installed, so a failure cannot be explained by never having submitted B.
+
+### Root cause and fix boundary
+
+- [search_tui.go:360](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/702440f9fe160cda6e6f0ce147a4c04c9e9f8d88/cmd/entire/cli/search_tui.go#L360): `searchResultsMsg` is accepted unconditionally.
+- [search_tui.go:381](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/702440f9fe160cda6e6f0ce147a4c04c9e9f8d88/cmd/entire/cli/search_tui.go#L381): an old page is also accepted unconditionally.
+- [search_tui.go:434](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/702440f9fe160cda6e6f0ce147a4c04c9e9f8d88/cmd/entire/cli/search_tui.go#L434): code search already rejects obsolete messages using a generation counter. Reuse that pattern for semantic search rather than inventing a framework.
+
+Proposed coherent PR scope:
+
+1. Tag both semantic response message types with a request generation.
+2. Advance the generation on a newly submitted semantic search, including repo/filter changes and re-submitting the same text.
+3. Reject obsolete messages before mutating any model field.
+4. Test late initial success, page success, errors, warnings and an empty old page; verify active-generation responses still work and page/loading state is not corrupted.
+5. Keep cancellation of superseded HTTP requests an optional separately justified extension; generation checking is required even if cancellation is added.
+
+### Existing-work check
+
+No exact public match was found in issue/PR searches for search + `late response`, `old query`, or semantic + `generation`. Related open PRs were inspected, including [#1960](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1960) (search IDs/telemetry; its TUI patch clears a correlation ID) and [#1943](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1943) (response size/per-cell errors); neither supplies request-generation isolation. This is evidence from public searches, not a guarantee against unannounced internal work.
+
+### Draft issue title and summary
+
+**Search TUI accepts late semantic responses from superseded queries**
+
+The code-search pane already guards against obsolete responses, but the semantic pane does not. A slow search A can finish after a newer search B and overwrite B's rows while B remains the current query. Old page responses also append A's rows and increment B's page. The attached deterministic regression tests reproduce both cases on the audited commit. Proposed fix: apply the existing generation-counter pattern to semantic first-page and pagination messages, rejecting stale messages before touching results, errors, warnings or loading/page state. May I contribute this scoped fix?
+
+## 2. Explicit checkpoint resume misses checkpoints merged through a second parent
+
+### Reproduction
+
+1. Create a feature commit with a real stored checkpoint and an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer.
+2. Merge the feature into `master` using `--no-ff`.
+3. Delete the merged feature branch.
+4. Check out an unrelated branch created before the feature.
+5. Run `entire checkpoint resume --checkpoint abc123def456`.
+
+Git's independent containment check reports:
+
+```text
+git branch --contains <checkpointed-feature-commit>
+  master
+```
+
+Entire reports:
+
+```text
+Checkpoint abc123def456 is not on any local branch; restoring session logs without switching branches.
+```
+
+The conversation is restored, but HEAD remains on the unrelated branch. The command promises to resume at a containing branch's current tip; this is not a request to restore stale code or add a snapshot-review workflow.
+
+### Controls
+
+| History | Expected routing | Observed |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Merge commit, feature deleted | Containing branch | Fails; remains on unrelated branch |
+| Merge commit, feature retained | An existing containing branch | Passes; switches to feature |
+| Fast-forward merge, feature deleted | Containing branch | Passes; switches to master |
+
+The failing case and both controls were repeated three times.
+
+### Cause and implementation caution
+
+[checkpoint_resume.go:213](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/702440f9fe160cda6e6f0ce147a4c04c9e9f8d88/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint_resume.go#L213) uses the picker's bounded branch index as a definitive containment check. [resume_picker.go:380](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/702440f9fe160cda6e6f0ce147a4c04c9e9f8d88/cmd/entire/cli/resume_picker.go#L380) walks only parent zero, so the checkpoint trailer on the merged feature is invisible after its branch is removed.
+
+Do not solve this by replacing every picker lookup with a full per-branch history scan. Prefer an explicit-target containment resolution that preserves the existing picker latency constraints; include real linked-worktree routing tests and distinguish an incomplete lookup from proof of absence.
+
+### Existing-work overlap
+
+- [#1727](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1727) is open and fixes a related first-parent problem in **listing/explanation**. Its changed files are `explain.go` and `explain_test.go`, not the resume branch index. Coordinate/reference it rather than claim the graph-traversal problem is novel.
+- [#2654](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2654) broadens session resume to share checkpoint resume's resolver. Its patch retains this `buildCheckpointBranchIndex` lookup; it does not fix the reproduced merge case.
+
+## 3. Search's real merge output disables the TUI's pagination
+
+**Status: reproduced client-side integration gap; verify the live service pagination contract before choosing a production fix.**
+
+The merge constructs `Total` from the number of rows retained after its per-type cap, while separately reporting capped facets in `CountsLowerBound`. The TUI treats `len(results) >= total` as exhaustive and returns no next-page command, ignoring those lower-bound signals.
+
+Reproduction feeds two valid one-row regional responses into the actual merge with limit 1, then passes its result into the actual TUI model. The merge retains one result and reports that commits are a lower bound. The UI nevertheless refuses to fetch:
+
+```text
+merge says commits are a lower bound, but TUI cannot fetch more:
+rows=1 total=1 lowerBound=map[commits:true]
+```
+
+- [search_v4.go:692](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/702440f9fe160cda6e6f0ce147a4c04c9e9f8d88/cmd/entire/cli/search_v4.go#L692): per-type cap.
+- [search_v4.go:704](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/702440f9fe160cda6e6f0ce147a4c04c9e9f8d88/cmd/entire/cli/search_v4.go#L704): total derived from retained rows.
+- [search_tui.go:595](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/702440f9fe160cda6e6f0ce147a4c04c9e9f8d88/cmd/entire/cli/search_tui.go#L595): pagination stops based on that total.
+
+[#2138](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2138) explicitly promises continuous scroll and next-page fetching. Existing TUI tests exercise that feature using manually supplied totals larger than the loaded rows, bypassing the actual merge output.
+
+Important: merely changing the stop condition is not a complete cross-cell fix. Rows discarded by the global cap may already have been consumed from a region's page. Establish page/cursor semantics and buffering first, including no missing/duplicate rows and bounded termination. Also distinguish coverage-incomplete counts from counts that actually imply another retrievable page. This is a larger follow-up than candidate 1, not a safe one-line PR.
+
+No exact public search-pagination issue or open fetch-ahead fix was found. [#1943](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1943) changes response-size and error handling, not this TUI stop condition.
+
+## Competitor checks: use them as workflow evidence, not feature-copying
+
+- [Cursor Origin Browse & Search](https://cursor.com/docs/origin/browse) documents repository search, branch selection and branch/author history browsing. This makes trustworthy current-query results a relevant competitive workflow; it does not establish that Cursor is free of stale-response bugs.
+- [Code Storage's documentation index](https://code.storage/docs/llms.txt) documents exact-version memory loading, agent-state capture/restore, parallel attempts from a common commit and paginated repository search. Those suggest testing exact identity, continuation and pagination. The individual restore/parallel Markdown pages were inaccessible through the browser tool; detailed implementation claims were not inferred from them.
+- [Cloudflare Artifacts best practices](https://developers.cloudflare.com/artifacts/concepts/best-practices/) emphasizes separate lifecycles for isolated agent work, stable-baseline forks, narrow tokens and metadata in Git notes. It supports testing that Entire routes a restored conversation to the correct worktree/branch; it is not a reason to add cross-session editing warnings.
+
+We are not proposing a storage-engine rewrite, mandatory file-overlap notifications, or immutable live-review snapshots.

Bro, I found concrete failures this time—and wrote tests that reproduce them.

I audited fresh upstream commit `702440f9f`, separately from your working branch. **My recommendation for our first contribution is #1 below.**

### 1. A slow search can overwrite a newer search’s results

Example:

1. Search for `payments`.
2. Before it finishes, search for `authentication`.
3. Authentication results arrive.
4. The older payments response arrives—and replaces them.

The current query remains `authentication`, but its results now belong to `payments`.

I also reproduced another variant: an old pagination response appends its results to the newer query and advances the newer query’s page counter.

**Why it happens:** semantic-search responses carry no request-generation identity. Code search already has that protection.

**Good PR scope:** apply the existing generation-check pattern to semantic results and pagination, including stale errors, warnings and loading-state changes. This is a contained correctness fix with meaningful regression coverage.

I checked related open search PRs, including [#1960](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1960) and [#1943](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1943); neither implements this protection. Public searches found no exact report, though that cannot rule out internal work.

### 2. Checkpoint resume restores a conversation on the wrong branch after merging

Reproduced sequence:

```text
Create feature commit with checkpoint
Merge feature into master using --no-ff
Delete feature branch
Switch to unrelated branch
Resume that checkpoint
```

Git confirms the checkpoint’s commit belongs to `master`. Entire instead prints:

```text
Checkpoint … is not on any local branch;
restoring session logs without switching branches.
```

It restores the conversation while leaving you on the unrelated branch.

**Cause:** its branch index follows only the first parent, missing the merged feature’s history.

Controls passed: fast-forward merging works; keeping the feature branch works.

**Overlap caveat:** [#1727](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1727) addresses a related graph-traversal bug in listing/explanation, not this resume lookup. [#2654](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2654) retains the faulty lookup. This deserves coordination, not a claim that nobody noticed merge-history problems.

### 3. Search pagination stops even when its own metadata says more results exist

I connected the actual cross-region merge output to the actual search UI model.

The merge returns:

```text
loaded rows: 1
total: 1
commits count is a lower bound: true
```

The UI sees `loaded >= total` and refuses to fetch another page, ignoring the lower-bound signal.

**Important:** this is a reproduced client-side integration gap, but its production fix needs confirmation of server pagination semantics. Simply changing the stopping condition could still skip rows discarded during cross-region merging. I would investigate this after #1.

### What the competitors contributed to this audit

- **Cursor Origin:** repository search and branch/author history browsing reinforce why trustworthy search results matter. [Documentation](https://cursor.com/docs/origin/browse)
- **Code Storage:** its documented exact-version restore and paginated-search workflows informed the continuation and pagination checks. [Documentation index](https://code.storage/docs/llms.txt)
- **Cloudflare Artifacts:** isolated agent-work lifecycles informed the branch/worktree-routing checks. [Best practices](https://developers.cloudflare.com/artifacts/concepts/best-practices/)

These are workflow comparisons—not claims that competitors have no equivalent bugs.

**Verification:** all three failures reproduced across three runs. Existing related tests pass. No production fixes or public issues/PRs were created; your working tree is unchanged.

[Full evidence and draft first issue](/private/tmp/entire-bug-audit.vgPAVn/REPORT.md) · [Runnable reproduction tests](/private/tmp/entire-bug-audit.vgPAVn/source/cmd/entire/cli/contribution_audit_repro_test.go)

**Start with stale semantic-search responses.** Their [contribution guide](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#before-you-code-discuss-first) requests an issue and maintainer approval before implementation. We now have the reproduction and scoped proposal to make that discussion concrete.

*** Add File: /private/tmp/entire-bug-audit.vgPAVn/TEN-MORE-BUGS.md
+# Ten additional Entire CLI findings — 2026-10-23
+
+## Scope and confidence
+
+- Audited fresh upstream main: `d1e19ab6ffa23851522847f47da49b0b99eab9e4`.
+- These exclude the three previous findings: superseded semantic-search responses, search pagination/merge integration, and merged-history checkpoint resume.
+- Ten regression tests reproduce ten additional failure classes. All ten fail consistently across three runs against unmodified production code. The SSE cursor test includes two related failing cases, counted as ONE bug.
+- Existing focused tests pass. No full CI/lint claim, no paid agent E2E calls, no production fixes, no published issues or PRs.
+- Work is in an isolated temporary checkout. The user's original working tree remains clean.
+- A reproduced defect is not proof of frequent field impact, maintainers' preferred behavior, or absence of unpublished work. Priorities below reflect those differences.
+
+## Ranked shortlist
+
+| Rank | Finding | Contribution judgment |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| 1 | Runner tailoring overwrites a concurrent configuration edit | Strong correctness contribution; clear preservation invariant |
+| 2 | Experts' staged scopes corrupt literal Git filenames | Strong contained contribution; Unicode and whitespace coverage |
+| 3 | A failed diagnostic bundle destroys an existing destination archive | Useful error-path/data-preservation fix |
+| 4 | Idle MCP server ignores context cancellation | Useful lifecycle fix; validate signal behavior as part of implementation |
+| 5 | Log following silently misses bytes after same-file truncation | Useful operational fix; bounded reproducible test |
+| 6 | Suggested patch cannot add the first line to an existing empty file | Reproduced CLI rejection; coordinate the empty-anchor API contract |
+| 7 | Trail-watch cursor handling drops ID-only updates and cannot clear an ID | Reproduced protocol edge case; live server emission frequency unverified |
+| 8 | Trail-watch JSON output changes large integer values | Reproduced data-integrity edge case; no claim deployed event IDs reach the boundary |
+| 9 | Typed API parameters silently round integers above int64 | Reproduced passthrough edge case; lower priority than ordinary workflows |
+| 10 | Token subtraction does not honor the nested-token depth guard | Reproduced defensive-programming defect; coordinate active token work |
+
+The lower-ranked edge cases are not ten equally urgent daily PRs. Start with the top few, and keep one coherent fix per PR.
+
+## 1. Runner tailoring silently undoes edits made while generation runs
+
+**Example:** `.entire/runners/risk.json` initially has `enabled: true`. `entire runner setup` reads it and starts generating a tailored prompt. While that runs, the user changes `enabled` to `false`. Applying the proposal writes the entire OLD JSON snapshot with its new prompt, resetting `enabled` to `true`.
+
+**Reproduction:** `TestDeepAuditRunnerTailoringPreservesConcurrentEdit` loads the actual runner, constructs a proposal with `replaceRunnerTemplate`, edits the on-disk setting, then calls the actual `applyTunedRunners`.
+
+Observed file:
+
+```json
+{"id":"risk","enabled":true,"prompt":{"template":"tailored template"}}
+```
+
+**Cause:** [runner_apply.go:114](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/d1e19ab6ffa23851522847f47da49b0b99eab9e4/cmd/entire/cli/runner_apply.go#L114) writes `c.newRaw`, derived from the earlier snapshot, without checking the current file. Atomic rename prevents a partially written JSON document, but does NOT prevent this lost update.
+
+**Fix direction:** detect changed/deleted/replaced files before applying the proposal. Conservatively refuse a stale proposal, or rebase only the template change onto a current document under an explicitly defined conflict policy. Do not promise a universal filesystem compare-and-swap against arbitrary editors; use existing locking/pre-image patterns where available and document the concurrency boundary.
+
+**Regression matrix:** unchanged file succeeds; non-template edit survives or causes refusal; concurrent template edit causes refusal; deleted file is not silently recreated; new/replaced runner is not overwritten; a stale member of a multi-runner batch is clearly reported.
+
+**Existing work:** public runner/stale/concurrent searches found no exact fix. Open [#2338](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2338) was checked; its changed files do not include `runner_apply.go`.
+
+## 2. `experts --staged` sends paths Git did not stage
+
+Stage `café.go` and ` leading.go`, then obtain the experts scopes.
+
+Actual:
+
+```text
+["leading.go", "\"caf\\303\\251.go\""]
+```
+
+The Unicode name remains Git's quoted representation rather than the real filename; the leading space is removed. The downstream provenance request therefore targets nonexistent or different paths.
+
+**Cause:** [experts_cmd.go:588](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/d1e19ab6ffa23851522847f47da49b0b99eab9e4/cmd/entire/cli/experts_cmd.go#L588) uses newline-delimited `git diff --cached --name-only`; `parseGitStagedScopeLines` then trims each filename instead of preserving its literal bytes.
+
+**Reproduction:** `TestDeepAuditExpertsStagedPaths` creates a real temporary repo and stages both real files before calling `stagedExpertScopes`.
+
+**Fix direction:** request `-z` and parse NUL-delimited literal paths without whitespace trimming. Test Unicode, leading/trailing whitespace, tabs, newlines and renames. Confirm the commands' read-only index behavior while touching this path.
+
+**Existing work:** [#2586](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2586) fixes a similar filename problem in checkpoint commit hooks, not this command. Its files are `strategy/manual_commit_hooks.go` and `strategy/mid_turn_commit_test.go`; no experts file is changed. Reference that precedent instead of claiming the whole filename class is new.
+
+## 3. A failed bundle overwrites a previously good diagnostic archive
+
+**Example:** save a useful `support.zip`. Retry `doctor bundle --out support.zip` while a source-access problem exists. The new attempt errors, but the previous archive is already gone.
+
+**Reproduction:** `TestDeepAuditBundleFailurePreservesDestination` uses an isolated output containing a marker and a temporary source with an invalid `.entire` path. `writeDoctorBundle` returns an error but replaces the old bytes with a 22-byte empty ZIP footer.
+
+**Cause:** [doctor_bundle.go:105](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/d1e19ab6ffa23851522847f47da49b0b99eab9e4/cmd/entire/cli/doctor_bundle.go#L105) opens the destination with `O_TRUNC` before reading source files or completing the archive.
+
+**Fix direction:** build/finalize/close a private temporary archive in the destination directory, and replace the requested output only after success. Preserve the previous archive on source, redaction, compression or close failure. Audit cancellation, permissions and temp cleanup. This finding does not say successful explicit `--out` must never overwrite a file.
+
+**Existing work:** [#2053](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2053), the atomic replacement refactor, was inspected; it does not change `doctor_bundle.go`. No exact bundle-failure clobber fix was found in public searches.
+
+## 4. Cancelling an idle MCP server does not stop it
+
+**Example:** an agent host launches `entire mcp` and leaves its stdin pipe open. SIGINT/SIGTERM cancels Entire's root context, but the MCP loop is blocked waiting for its next line and does not return.
+
+**Reproduction:** `TestDeepAuditIdleMCPCancellation` gives the actual `runMCPServer` an open `io.Pipe` and cancels its context with no input. It remains blocked; closing stdin releases it. No real MCP host or external API is required.
+
+**Cause:** [mcp.go:85](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/d1e19ab6ffa23851522847f47da49b0b99eab9e4/cmd/entire/cli/mcp.go#L85) passes context into dispatch but never makes its blocking `Scanner.Scan` interruptible. Main catches the first terminating signal and cancels context rather than immediately exiting, so the command must cooperate.
+
+**Fix direction:** make idle input waiting cancellable at the owned transport boundary and return the cancellation cause. Do not merely add a check inside the loop: it cannot run while Scan is blocked. Avoid leaking a blocked reader goroutine or closing a caller-owned reader unexpectedly.
+
+**Implementation verification:** real subprocess tests for idle SIGINT/SIGTERM, correct exit outcome, normal EOF and normal requests; retain existing JSON-RPC framing tests.
+
+**Existing work:** searches for MCP cancellation/hangs and `runMCPServer` found its original implementation [#1585](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1585), not an active focused fix.
+
+## 5. `doctor logs --follow` gets stuck after copy-truncation
+
+**Example:** while following a log, a user clears it or a log manager uses copytruncate. New log entries are appended to the SAME inode. Entire keeps the old byte offset, so it silently misses new entries until the file grows beyond that old position.
+
+**Reproduction:** `TestDeepAuditFollowLogTruncation` first waits for a real appended marker to prove the follower is running. It then truncates that same file and writes a shorter new marker. Four polling intervals pass without that marker being emitted; reproduced three times.
+
+**Cause:** [doctor_logs.go:124](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/d1e19ab6ffa23851522847f47da49b0b99eab9e4/cmd/entire/cli/doctor_logs.go#L124) repeatedly reads one descriptor and treats every EOF as temporary; it never detects size shrinking below its offset.
+
+**Fix direction:** detect truncation and reset the offset before following new bytes. Define rename/replacement behavior separately. Do not conflate this with the descriptor-vs-name choice of `tail -f` versus `tail -F`.
+
+**Caveat:** the current logger does not appear to perform automatic rotation; a comment in `doctor_logs.go` says it does, but that is not evidence of an implementation. This report uses explicit file truncation, not an invented automatic rotation path.
+
+**Existing work:** no focused public `followFile`, copytruncate or doctor-log-follow fix was found.
+
+## 6. A valid patch to an existing empty file is rejected
+
+Track an empty `empty.txt`, then suggest:
+
+```diff
+--- a/empty.txt
++++ b/empty.txt
+@@ -0,0 +1 @@
++hello
+```
+
+Native `git apply --check` accepts it. Entire's actual anchor resolver rejects it:
+
+```text
+empty.txt: patch expects lines 1-1 but the file has 0
+```
+
+**Cause:** [trail_review_patch.go:292](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/d1e19ab6ffa23851522847f47da49b0b99eab9e4/cmd/entire/cli/trail_review_patch.go#L292), together with the target parser's clamping of line 0 to line 1, cannot represent an empty pre-image. This file exists; it is not the deliberately unsupported `/dev/null` new-file case.
+
+**Reproduction:** `TestDeepAuditPatchIntoExistingEmptyFile` validates the fixture with native Git before calling the actual resolver.
+
+**Fix direction / uncertainty:** preserve an empty pre-image with the file's hash and an explicit insertion anchor. Confirm the entire-api suggested-change contract supports that representation; an end-to-end fix may need coordinated server work. Until confirmed, this is not promised as a CLI-only daily PR.
+
+**Existing work:** no exact existing-empty-file patch fix was found in public issue/PR searches.
+
+## 7. Trail-watch reconnect cursor mishandles control frames
+
+Two related cases, counted as one defect:
+
+- An ID-only block (`id: 23` followed by a blank line) is discarded; the cursor is not updated.
+- An explicit empty `id:` does not clear the previous cursor.
+
+The [SSE parsing standard](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html#parsing-an-event-stream) defines persistent ID-buffer updates, including an empty value. The code itself promises to return the last observed `id:` for reconnect.
+
+**Cause:** [trail_watch_cmd.go:233](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/d1e19ab6ffa23851522847f47da49b0b99eab9e4/cmd/entire/cli/trail_watch_cmd.go#L233) only advances the cursor while flushing an event with content, and only if the ID is non-empty. The reconnect caller also discards an empty returned cursor.
+
+**Reproduction:** `TestDeepAuditSSECursorControlFrames` drives the real stream parser with a fake HTTP server. Actual cursors are empty instead of `23`, and `23` instead of empty, respectively.
+
+**Fix direction:** separate persistent cursor state from per-event fields; distinguish no ID update from an explicit clear, and carry that meaning through reconnect. Test the next HTTP request's actual `Last-Event-ID` header, not only the parser return value.
+
+**Caveat:** no claim that today's deployed Entire server regularly emits these control-frame shapes. This is a confirmed parser edge case, not measured production incident frequency.
+
+## 8. Trail-watch JSON output changes large integers
+
+Input:
+
+```json
+{"id":9007199254740993}
+```
+
+Actual `--json` event data:
+
+```json
+{"id":9007199254740992}
+```
+
+**Cause:** [trail_watch_cmd.go:356](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/d1e19ab6ffa23851522847f47da49b0b99eab9e4/cmd/entire/cli/trail_watch_cmd.go#L356) unmarshals the payload into `any`, converting numbers to float64, then marshals it again. Values beyond exact float64 integer precision change silently.
+
+**Reproduction:** `TestDeepAuditSSEJSONPreservesInteger` inspects the encoded output using `json.Number`, not float64, so its assertion does not repeat the production bug.
+
+**Fix direction:** embed validated `json.RawMessage`, or decode with `UseNumber` when structural manipulation is required. Test nested numeric fields, small numbers, invalid JSON fallback and large signed/unsigned integers.
+
+**Caveat:** deployed event IDs may currently be strings or small integers; no claim that they already cross this boundary. The defect is in the JSON passthrough contract.
+
+## 9. `entire api -F` silently rounds large integer inputs
+
+Input flag:
+
+```text
+-F value=9223372036854775809
+```
+
+Actual request body:
+
+```json
+{"value":9223372036854776000}
+```
+
+**Cause:** [api_cmd.go:297](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/d1e19ab6ffa23851522847f47da49b0b99eab9e4/cmd/entire/cli/api_cmd.go#L297) tries signed int64, then float64. An integer outside signed int64 becomes a rounded float rather than an exact numeric value or a clear refusal.
+
+**Reproduction:** `TestDeepAuditAPITypedLargeInteger` builds fields through the actual helper and reads the actual generated request body. The integer is valid JSON; the test does not require the illustrative endpoint to exist.
+
+**Fix direction:** preserve valid numeric spelling using `json.Number` with JSON-number validation, or define and enforce an explicit range error. Do not silently send a different value. Test POST and explicit GET, int64 boundaries, large unsigned values, exponent/decimal syntax, and non-JSON float spellings such as NaN.
+
+**Caveat:** this is a lower-priority generic passthrough edge case, not a demonstrated failing high-volume Entire endpoint. `-f` or an explicit body can be a workaround when a string/raw JSON is appropriate.
+
+## 10. Token subtraction lacks the addition path's recursion guard
+
+**Observed:** a 24-deep child-usage chain remains 24 deep after subtraction, although `MaxSubagentDepth` is 16 and addition clips to that guard.
+
+**Cause:** [agent/types/token_usage.go:127](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/d1e19ab6ffa23851522847f47da49b0b99eab9e4/cmd/entire/cli/agent/types/token_usage.go#L127) threads `depth` through recursive subtraction but never checks it. The addition path does check it. Subtraction is used in actual checkpoint-window token scoping.
+
+**Reproduction:** `TestDeepAuditSubtractionHonorsDepthLimit` uses only a small synthetic in-memory chain. No large payload, stack exhaustion or destructive resource test was run.
+
+**Fix direction:** apply a consistent depth policy to subtraction while preserving normal totals, operand immutability and coverage markers. Add exact-boundary and beyond-boundary tests. Treat this as defensive robustness; no field exploit or severity is claimed. If assessment shows a security impact through shared input, follow SECURITY.md rather than opening a public exploit report.
+
+**Existing work / coordination:** active [#2825](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2825) and [#2155](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2155) change the same token types. Their fetched patches do not introduce this subtraction-depth check, but coordinate a minimal change rather than compete with their accounting/model work.
+
+## What was excluded
+
+- Previous three findings, as requested.
+- Active work on checkpoint queue generation, privacy gating, token-counting semantics, worktree homes/settings and checkpoint filename matching.
+- A colon-prefixed rename destination is mishandled by `parseDiffTreeOutput` when directly fed an R100 record, but the current public diff helper still returned both paths in the native fixture. This is a latent parser defect without a reproduced current product failure, so it is NOT counted among these ten.
+- Rename-based log following was replaced with the stronger same-inode truncation case, avoiding confusion with intentional descriptor-following semantics.
+
+## Competitor grounding
+
+This audit uses competitors to identify contracts worth preserving, not to invent ten feature requests:
+
+- [Code Storage's index](https://code.storage/docs/llms.txt) explicitly describes expected-ref guards for safe notes retries (`expected_notes_ref_sha`) and exact-source guards for merges. The relevant lesson for runner tailoring is optimistic concurrency: an atomic write is not sufficient protection against a stale pre-image.
+- [Cursor Origin](https://cursor.com/docs/origin) documents repositories, review and agent/automation integration. Reliable path identity and applicable suggested changes are relevant workflow-quality properties; no claim is made about Cursor's internal implementations or absence of equivalent defects.
+- [Cloudflare Artifacts best practices](https://developers.cloudflare.com/artifacts/concepts/best-practices/) emphasizes isolated work lifecycles and independently reviewable/mergeable units. Safe cancellation, reliable diagnostics and avoiding unintended configuration updates support those workflows without adding session-overlap warnings.
+
+## Reproduction files and commands
+
+Ten counted tests:
+
+- `/private/tmp/entire-bug-audit.vgPAVn/source/cmd/entire/cli/contribution_audit_deep_repro_test.go` — nine CLI findings.
+- `/private/tmp/entire-bug-audit.vgPAVn/source/cmd/entire/cli/agent/types/contribution_audit_deep_repro_test.go` — token-depth finding.
+
+Run from the isolated checkout:
+
+```sh
+GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.27.3 GOCACHE=/private/tmp/entire-bug-audit.vgPAVn/go-cache GOMAXPROCS=4 go test -p 4 ./cmd/entire/cli ./cmd/entire/cli/agent/types -run '^TestDeepAudit' -count=3 -timeout=30s
+```
+
+All ten fail on unmodified upstream, as intentional regression reproductions. The pipeline is not ready to merge while those tests are red.
+
+Existing related tests passed:
+
+```sh
+GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.27.3 GOCACHE=/private/tmp/entire-bug-audit.vgPAVn/go-cache GOMAXPROCS=4 go test -p 4 ./cmd/entire/cli ./cmd/entire/cli/agent/types -run '^(TestStagedExpert|TestParseGitStaged|TestLocalExpert|TestResolveTrailReview|TestPatch|TestStreamOnce|TestReplaceRunner|TestApplyTuned|TestMCP|TestPrintTail|TestReadLastNLines|TestFollow|TestWriteDoctorBundle|TestBuildAPI|TestInfer|TestTokenUsage|TestAddTokenUsage|TestSubtractTokenUsage)' -count=1 -timeout=60s
+```
+
+Public searches and selected related PR patches were checked on 2026-10-23. No exact active fixes for these reproduced failure cases were identified; this is not a guarantee about unannounced work. Confirm scope with maintainers using a short reproduction before implementing, per CONTRIBUTING.md.
+
+## Suggested first issue
+
+**Title:** Runner tailoring can overwrite configuration edits made while generation is running
+
+`runner setup` loads each runner's raw JSON before generation. If the file changes while generation is running, `applyTunedRunners` writes the old full document plus the generated template without checking the current contents. A deterministic regression test changes `enabled:true` to `enabled:false` after loading; applying the proposal returns success and re-enables the runner. I propose detecting a changed pre-image and refusing the stale proposal, with tests for non-template edits, template edits and deleted/replaced files. Is this an acceptable scope for a contribution?
*** End Patch"));

Found **10 additional reproducible failures** on fresh upstream `d1e19ab6f`, excluding the previous three.

I wrote regression tests: all ten reproduced across three runs; existing focused tests passed. Your original checkout is untouched.

The [full audit report](/private/tmp/entire-bug-audit.vgPAVn/TEN-MORE-BUGS.md) includes pinned source links, reproduction details, fix directions, related-PR checks and caveats.

## Strongest contribution targets

### 1. Runner tailoring silently overwrites configuration edits

`runner setup` loads a runner’s JSON, then spends time generating its tailored prompt.

During generation, change `enabled: true` to `false`. When tailoring finishes, it writes the old document with the new prompt—**silently restoring `enabled: true`.**

Cause: applying a stale full-file snapshot without checking whether the file changed.

Contribution: detect stale input and refuse or safely reconcile it. Cover edited, deleted and replaced files—not just the happy path.

This is unrelated to our dropped session-overlap proposal: no warnings about agents editing shared files.

### 2. `experts --staged` corrupts real filenames

I staged two actual files:

```text
café.go
 leading.go
```

The command produced scopes equivalent to:

```text
"caf\303\251.go"
leading.go
```

One remains Git’s quoted representation; the other loses its leading space. Provenance lookup therefore receives incorrect paths.

Contribution: use NUL-delimited Git output and preserve filenames literally; test Unicode, whitespace, tabs, newlines and renames.

Related [PR #2586](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2586) addresses checkpoint hooks, **not this experts command**.

### 3. Failed diagnostic bundles destroy the previous archive

You have a useful `support.zip`. Run another bundle into that destination, but source collection encounters an unreadable log directory.

The command errors—yet the previous archive has already been truncated. My reproduction left a **22-byte empty ZIP**.

The fixture passes normal `.entire` validation; this is not merely a rejected malformed-directory case.

Contribution: finish a temporary archive successfully before replacing the destination, preserving the previous archive on failure.

### 4. An idle MCP server ignores cancellation

With stdin open but idle, cancelling `runMCPServer`’s context does not stop it. Closing stdin releases it.

Cause: blocking `Scanner.Scan()` cannot observe cancellation. Given Entire’s signal handler, this can prevent graceful shutdown after the first termination signal.

Contribution: cancellable transport handling with tests for idle cancellation, EOF and normal requests. Avoid leaving a blocked reader goroutine behind.

### 5. Log following misses new entries after truncation

While `doctor logs --follow` runs:

1. Append a marker and confirm it appears.
2. Truncate that same file.
3. Append a shorter new entry.

Entire retains the old offset and misses the new entry until the file grows past that position.

Contribution: detect shrinking files and reset the offset. This reproduction concerns **same-file truncation**, not disputed rename/rotation semantics.

## More findings—with narrower impact

### 6. Valid patches to existing empty files are rejected

For an existing empty file:

```diff
@@ -0,0 +1 @@
+hello
```

Native `git apply --check` accepts it. Entire’s suggested-patch resolver reports:

```text
patch expects lines 1-1 but the file has 0
```

Contribution: represent empty pre-images correctly. First confirm the server’s suggested-change contract supports the required insertion anchor.

### 7. Trail-watch reconnect cursors mishandle SSE control frames

Two cases fail:

- An ID-only block does not update the reconnect cursor.
- An explicit empty `id:` cannot clear the previous cursor.

Both behaviors conflict with the [SSE parsing rules](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html#parsing-an-event-stream).

Contribution: preserve cursor state independently of displayed events, including explicit clearing. **Current production frequency is unverified.**

### 8. Trail-watch JSON output silently changes large integers

Input:

```json
{"id":9007199254740993}
```

Output contains:

```json
{"id":9007199254740992}
```

Cause: decoding through `float64` before re-encoding.

Contribution: preserve raw JSON or use `json.Number`. This is a demonstrated passthrough defect, not evidence that deployed IDs currently reach that size.

### 9. `entire api -F` sends a different integer than requested

Input:

```text
-F value=9223372036854775809
```

Generated request:

```json
{"value":9223372036854776000}
```

Cause: signed-integer parsing fails, then floating-point parsing silently rounds.

Contribution: preserve valid numeric spelling or reject unsupported ranges explicitly. Lower priority than the ordinary-workflow failures above.

### 10. Token subtraction bypasses the existing nesting guard

Token addition respects `MaxSubagentDepth = 16`; subtraction does not.

A small 24-level fixture remains 24 levels deep after subtraction. The recursive helper receives a depth parameter but never checks it.

Contribution: consistent depth handling and boundary tests. This is defensive hardening, not a claimed exploit. Active [#2825](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2825) and [#2155](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2155) touch token types, so coordinate before implementing.

## What I would pick

**Start with #1, then #2 and #3.** They demonstrate useful engineering judgment: preserving user edits, preserving path identity and preserving existing data.

The competitor comparison is in the report. Particularly relevant: Code Storage documents expected-ref guards for stale updates—the same underlying distinction here between an atomic write and a safe update. [Code Storage documentation](https://code.storage/docs/llms.txt)

I found no exact active fixes for these cases in the public searches checked, but that cannot rule out unpublished work. These are ten reproduced failures—not ten equally valuable PRs. The first three are where I would spend our contribution time.

### A. #2580 — Git config-based hook delivery

**Best larger systems contribution found.** It replaces recurring hook-file ownership fights with Git-native configuration. Git's [2.54 documentation](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-hook/2.54.0.html) confirms config-defined hook events and traditional-hook coexistence.

A meaningful first slice must handle:

1. Capability detection, plus safe behavior when command-line Git and a GUI's older bundled Git operate on the same clone.
2. Exactly-once Entire execution while legacy/config/Lefthook paths coexist. Merely installing both doubles newer Git events.
3. Idempotent install and migration without deleting other tools' hooks/config.
4. Doctor/status inspection and disable/uninstall symmetry.
5. Normal/linked worktrees, core.hooksPath, arguments and pre-push stdin preservation; native Windows and Unix verification.

Start by getting agreement on fallback/dedup semantics and writing an acceptance matrix. Do not begin by replacing every hook backend or building a general plugin framework.

### B. #763 — capture declared pre-flight knowledge context

[Issue #763](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/763), opened by **totto**, association **NONE** (community/no repo affiliation shown). Open, no assignees, no comments/claims or implementing PR identified.

**Potentially substantial and aligned with LegionCode's context assembly**, but a product/schema proposal, not an independently reproduced bug. It asks to record the manifests/versions/hashes available when an agent runs, in addition to the conversation and resulting code.

Bounded first slice: optional, provider-neutral, versioned manifest metadata with stable IDs and content hashes; session-start association; checkpoint persistence; explain/export inspection; size limits, opt-in/redaction rules and old-checkpoint compatibility. Start with one explicit producer, not automatic crawling of AGENTS.md, every file and every retrieval system.

Important semantic boundary: a file present or declared available is **not proof that the model read or used it**. Capture level must be labelled honestly (declared / supplied / agent-reported), and avoid promising auditor-grade proof without instrumentation.

Maintainer approval is required before schema design/implementation. Do not make KCP a mandatory dependency merely because it appears in the report.

### C. #2794 — legacy checkpoint push interferes with user's push

[Issue #2794](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/2794), opened by **simon-scrl**, association **NONE**. Open, no assignees/comments/direct PR cross-reference or claim found.

None of these guarantees hiring, and a patch's line count is not its seniority. The convincing signal is a clear user failure, independently verified root cause, a deliberately bounded design, compatibility/migration consideration, failure/cancellation tests, and measured validation.

The audit is saved with the exclusions and ownership evidence. I found no clean pickup among the eight open issues publicly authored by org members/collaborators: each is assigned, already implemented or linked to ongoing work.

My recommendation is a bounded runner-safety fix to ship first, then #2580 as the larger project if maintainers agree. The JSON-number edge cases are useful fixes, but I wouldn’t present them as flagship contributions.

**Some are worthwhile contributions, but I would not sell all ten as senior-level projects.** The strongest opportunities are runner safety, MCP lifecycle correctness, and a larger Git-hook delivery project.

I checked **110 open issues, their timelines/comments, and 218 open PRs**, plus targeted searches of closed work. Today’s source check used upstream `d05c0a144`.

## 1. Are our ten findings already reported or being fixed?

“No exact match found” below means **a candidate for a new report**, not proof nobody has discovered it privately.

| Finding | Current public-work check | Contribution value |
|---|---|---|
| Runner tailoring overwrites configuration edits | No exact report/fix found. Related runner PR does not fix application of stale files. | **Strong bounded contribution** |
| `experts --staged` corrupts filenames | No exact experts fix found. [#2586](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2586) fixes checkpoint hooks, not experts. | Useful small–medium fix |
| Failed bundle destroys the previous archive | No exact fix found; atomic-JSON work does not cover ZIP output. | Useful data-preservation fix |
| Idle MCP ignores cancellation | No exact cancellation report/fix found. | **Strong lifecycle contribution** |
| Log following misses entries after truncation | No exact report/fix found. | Useful smaller operational fix |
| Suggested patch rejects an existing empty file | No exact fix found; server anchor contract needs agreement. | Medium, potentially cross-component |
| SSE reconnect cursor mishandling | No exact fix found; trail refactoring does not repair the parser. | Medium protocol fix; production relevance needs establishing |
| SSE JSON rounds large integers | No exact fix found. | Small edge-case fix |
| `api -F` rounds large integers | No exact fix found. | Small edge-case fix |
| Token subtraction lacks its depth guard | Exact check not found, but [#2825](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2825) and [#2155](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2155) modify this area. | Small hardening fix; **coordinate first** |

**My honest assessment:** runner and MCP fixes can demonstrate senior judgment if we handle failure modes properly. Two numeric conversions and a depth check are legitimate contributions, but not flagship projects.

## 2. Larger existing issues worth discussing

### A. #2580 — Git-native hook registration: strongest larger candidate

[Issue #2580](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/2580) proposes config-based hooks instead of competing with hook managers for `.git/hooks/*`.

- Author: `peyton-alt`
- Public association: `CONTRIBUTOR`; **team employment not established**
- Unassigned; no visible implementation claim/prototype
- No directly implementing PR found
- Related [#2388](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2388) handles Lefthook integration, so coordination matters

This is substantial because a correct implementation must address:

1. New command-line Git and older GUI-bundled Git sharing one clone.
2. Exactly-once execution while old and new delivery paths coexist.
3. Safe migration without deleting another tool’s hooks.
4. Matching install, doctor, status and uninstall behavior.
5. Worktrees, Windows, hook arguments and pre-push stdin.

Git’s configuration-based hooks are documented in the [Git 2.54 manual](https://git-scm.com/docs/git-hook/2.54.0.html).

**This is my preferred larger project.** A thoughtful compatibility design and migration test matrix would show substantially more than simply adding a command.

### B. #763 — Record pre-flight context manifests

[Issue #763](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/763) asks to preserve which knowledge manifests, versions and hashes were available when an agent ran.

- Author: `totto`
- Public association: `NONE`—community/no repository affiliation shown
- Unassigned; no comments, implementation claim or implementing PR found

This connects directly to your **LegionCode context-assembly experience**.

A credible first slice would include optional, versioned manifest metadata, hashes, session association, checkpoint persistence, explain/export output, size limits and privacy handling.

The important judgment call: **“available to the agent” is not proof “read or used by the model.”** We must label that distinction honestly.

This could become a substantial contribution, but it needs product/schema approval first—not speculative implementation.

### C. #2794 — Checkpoint pushes interfere with the user’s push

[Issue #2794](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/2794) is open, unassigned and has no directly linked PR or visible claimant.

- Author: `simon-scrl`
- Public association: `NONE`

However, **I would not call it clean independent work**. [#2715](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2715) already addresses the same push-ordering failure for the git-refs backend. The issue reports the legacy git-branch path.

Potential contribution: establish whether legacy coverage remains missing and coordinate an extension. Do not build a competing upload mechanism. The reported server race also still needs independent verification.

## 3. Team-authored versus community-authored

Public GitHub affiliation is not the same as employment, so I won’t invent that distinction.

**Org-member/maintainer bucket:** I checked all eight open issues authored by `MEMBER`/`COLLABORATOR` accounts. **None was a clean pickup under your filter.**

Examples:

- [#2202](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/2202): assigned, with implementation work.
- [#2197](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/2197): multiple PRs.
- [#2091](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/2091): performance umbrella with claims and overlapping PRs.
- [#1006](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/1006): no linked PR, but assigned to `pjbgf`.

**Community bucket:** #763 is the clearest larger unclaimed discussion candidate. #2794 needs coordination.

**Affiliation unknown:** #2580. Prior contributions alone do not establish that its author is inside or outside Entire.

## 4. Issues I deliberately rejected

This is where checking comments and code mattered:

- **#2718:** no PR, but the author already has working prototype branches.
- **#2673:** another contributor offers the implementation.
- **#2535:** an explicit contributor handoff already happened.
- **#2689:** parts overlap existing work; merged [#2692](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2692) removed the attribution machinery behind other parts.

**Ship runner-safety first; pursue #2580 as the larger project.** Keep #763 as the LegionCode-aligned design discussion.

Senior signal comes from the reproduction, design boundaries, compatibility decisions and verification—not PR size. Also, Entire explicitly requests [maintainer agreement before implementation](https://github.com/entireio/cli/blob/d05c0a14437fdc071ed97655ec41046018bd8d2e/CONTRIBUTING.md), so we should follow that rather than opening simultaneous issue/PR pairs to reserve work.

Audited commit: bd0c4d1d171bbd9246239be4d28ca8ef2b1d5680 (synced origin/main).

## 1. Recommended first contribution: checkpoint replay silently overwrites a remote session

Suggested issue title: **Checkpoint divergence recovery reports success after replacing another clone's session**

### Observable example

Two independent repositories hold the same checkpoint with one session, S0.
A and B independently append different sessions to that checkpoint:
- A appends SA and successfully pushes.
- B, still based on the original checkpoint, appends SB and flushes its push queue.
- B's first push is rejected as non-fast-forward. Entire fetches, replays and retries.
- Entire prints “pushed 1 of 1” and removes the checkpoint from the queue.
- The published checkpoint lists S0 and SB. SA has disappeared from the current checkpoint.

This does not require two sessions editing the same source file or sharing a worktree. It concerns metadata for an existing shared checkpoint. Adding another session to an existing checkpoint is supported; see resolveAttachCheckpoint in cmd/entire/cli/attach.go:453 and TestAttach_ReviewAppendsAsAdditionalSessionWhenIDDiffers in attach_test.go:1286. The reproduction invokes the persistent write surface used by those workflows, followed by the actual queue flush/recovery path. It does not drive the complete interactive attach command.

### Reproduction

Test: cmd/entire/cli/strategy/senior_sync_repro_test.go:64
Name: TestSeniorSync_RecoveryPreservesBothAttachedSessions

Uses actual git-refs stores in temporary repositories and a temporary bare remote. No hosted services or agent APIs.

Observed:
\`\`\`text
[entire] Checkpoint ref push failed; retrying 1 ref(s) individually... pushed 1 of 1
successful recovery removed a previously pushed session;
current sessions=[shared-session local-added-session]
\`\`\`

The strengthened test verifies the recovered local tip equals the bare remote's tip and the checkpoint is no longer queued. Therefore this is published bad checkpoint state, not just stale local display.

Important limit: the remote commit is preserved as an ancestor. The overwritten content can still exist in Git history; this is loss from the current checkpoint and its normal reads, not proof of permanently erased Git objects.

### Root cause

1. pushCheckpointRefWithRecovery (strategy/push_common.go:75) explicitly describes overlapping writes as a recovery error that should leave the ref queued.
2. Recovery calls cherryPickOnto (strategy/metadata_reconcile.go:408).
3. treeChangesForCherryPick/changeToTreeChange reduce changes to a destination path and replacement entry; the expected old entry is discarded.
4. checkpoint.ApplyTreeChanges (checkpoint/parse_tree.go:203) applies these replacements to the fetched tree without checking the original preimage against the remote entry.
5. Both independent appends allocate the next numbered session slot and change root metadata.json. Replay substitutes B's slot and root metadata over A's versions.

Git ancestry becomes a fast-forward, but logical checkpoint contents have not been safely merged.

### Meaningful first PR scope

- Implement checked replay using original/base, fetched/current and proposed entries.
- Preserve non-overlapping changes and make identical writes idempotent.
- Refuse incompatible add/add, modify/modify and delete/modify changes with an inspectable conflict error.
- On refusal, preserve the local update and remote tip, and leave the ref queued.
- Keep failures fail-soft for the user's ordinary code push.
- Add conflict tests using real checkpoint session layouts, alongside existing disjoint-file tests.
- Cover both per-checkpoint ref push recovery and other callers of the shared replay engine; do not claim untested callers are fixed.
- Document the recovery behavior. A future semantic union/reindex of independently appended sessions is a separate design decision; an initial fix should not invent JSON merge rules or silently discard one side.

The present failure test accepts a safe error and verifies remote preservation/queue retention. It should be strengthened further to pin the exact typed conflict and unchanged local ref on refusal when implementing the fix.

### Related work checked

- [#2876](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2876), open: pins exact queued generations and prevents concurrent local writers from being overwritten. Its current patch still calls the existing cherryPickOnto engine; it adds no content-conflict checking there. This audit has inspected that patch, not run the new test on that PR's branch.
- [#1638](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1638), open: test-only divergence/recovery matrix. Its description explicitly says a content-level cherry-pick conflict is not reproduced and uses remote rejection to exercise the queued-error behavior. The new reproduction supplies the missing case.
- [#1917](https://github.com/entireio/cli/issues/1917), closed, and [#2131](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2131), open: same-machine concurrent ref writes and CAS/batching. Cross-clone conflicting content is a separate invariant.
- [#1251](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1251), merged: avoids orphaning local commits by replaying onto a fetched ref. It does not make overlapping content replay conflict-aware.

No exact public issue or active implementation was located in the targeted searches as of this audit. That is a bounded search result, not a guarantee about private plans or every discussion. Link the related work in the issue and PR, and coordinate with the active recovery work.

### Why this can demonstrate senior engineering

The contribution is about preserving user data across distributed histories, designing conflict semantics, keeping refs/queues consistent on failure, and testing real storage and remote behavior. The number of changed lines is secondary. A tested safe-refusal fix is useful even before implementing automatic session merging.

## 2. Second contribution: generated summaries can be attached to the wrong session

Suggested issue title: **Checkpoint summary generation can write a session's summary onto a newly attached session**

### Observable example

- A checkpoint contains session S1.
- checkpoint explain --generate selects S1's transcript and starts its slow summary provider.
- Another legitimate operation appends S2 to the same checkpoint before generation completes.
- The provider returns a summary of S1.
- Entire reports successful generation, but saves that summary on S2. S1 receives no summary.

The test controls the interleaving by appending S2 inside the stub provider. It calls the actual generation/persistence path. No model call is made.

Test: cmd/entire/cli/senior_summary_repro_test.go:19
Name: TestSeniorSummary_GeneratedSummaryStaysWithItsSourceSession

Observed:
\`\`\`text
summary for session-001 was silently saved on unrelated session-002;
explain reported success: ✓ Summary generated for a1b2c3d4e5f6
the session actually sent to the generator did not receive its summary
\`\`\`

Runtime reproduction currently covers the git-branch backend. Both stores call the shared applySummaryBackfill routine, but the refs backend has not been independently reproduced in this audit.

### Root cause

- generateCheckpointSummary (cmd/entire/cli/explain.go:1033) reads a particular transcript before the provider call.
- At explain.go:1100 it writes checkpoint.SessionSummary with only CheckpointID and Summary.
- api/checkpoint/interfaces.go:84 defines that request as targeting the checkpoint's latest session, without a stable SessionID.
- treeWriter.applySummaryBackfill (checkpoint/persistent.go:234) calculates the latest session when the write executes.
- A session appended during generation changes the write target.

This is an integration contract bug: “latest at write time” cannot safely persist a result generated from “latest at read time.”

### Meaningful first PR scope

- Give the summary write a stable target session identity (extend the request or introduce a scoped request while explicitly preserving legacy semantics where required).
- Have the generator pass the selected source identity.
- Resolve that identity and write atomically inside the existing storage transaction.
- Define behavior when the source was removed or changed while generation ran; at minimum never retarget silently.
- Cover concurrent append, missing source, transcript change, existing-summary/force behavior and both backends.
- Consider a source transcript revision/digest to prevent stale content summaries; choose that separately from the minimum identity fix.
- Preserve redaction ordering and fan-out/routing behavior.

### Related work checked

Targeted searches included generateCheckpointSummary, applySummaryBackfill, summary plus concurrent/race, wrong session, source session and latest session.
- [#2796](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/2796), merged: repo redaction settings for summary writes. It does not address target identity.
- [#813](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/813), closed without merge: multi-session line-attribution aggregation; a different meaning of “summary.”
- Searches found no exact public issue/fix for this generation-to-write target race.

This is a real provenance bug, but narrower in impact than the checkpoint sync failure. It is a reasonable second contribution; do not inflate it into the primary distributed data-loss problem.

Start with conflict-aware checkpoint replay. Keep the first implementation focused on verified data preservation and explicit conflicts. Submit the minimal failing case, root-cause explanation, relation to existing recovery work, and a tested patch as one coherent contribution.
